chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'When I was taken on the night journey to the heaven, Gabriel brought me to a place which Gabriel had never trodden upon before. So it was unveiled to him, and God showed him — from the light of His magnificence — what He willed.'

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ: The passive form of sara, referring to the miraculous night journey (Isra) of the Prophet from Mecca to Jerusalem and thence to the heavens
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: The heavens or celestial realm to which the Prophet ascended during the Isra wal-Mi'raj
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Gabriel, the archangel who serves as divine messenger and who accompanied the Prophet on the ascension
key_terms.مَا أَحَبَّ: What He willed or loved — indicating that the revelation was according to God's own choosing, not bounded by Gabriel's limits
key_terms.نُورِ عَظَمَتِهِ: The light of His magnificence — a key phrase indicating a theophany bounded by divine will, used in Shia theology to affirm that God showed the Prophet something of His Greatness without implying corporealism

ai.seo_question: What did Allah show the Prophet during the night journey (Isra) when Gabriel could go no further?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a tradition attributed to Imam al-Rida (AS) about the Prophet's Isra (night journey), in which Gabriel accompanied the Prophet to the heavens but reached a point beyond which even Gabriel could not proceed. At that transcendent threshold, the veil was lifted and God manifested some of the light of His majesty to the Prophet as He willed. This narration underscores the unique spiritual station of the Prophet (SAWW), surpassing even the highest angels, and forms part of the theological discussion on Divine transcendence beyond creation.
word_analysis: I was taken on the night journey

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When I<sup>saww</sup> was ascended to the sky, Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> reached with me<sup>saww</sup> to a place which Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> had not trodden upon at all’. So it was uncovered for him<sup>saww</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Showed him<sup>saww</sup>, from the Light of His<sup>azwj</sup> magnificence, whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Loved to’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu Nasr from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.)

who has said that the holy Prophet (s.a.) said, “When Jibril took me for a visit to the heavens we reached a place where he had never sat food there before. Then it was unveiled to him and Allah showed him of the light of His greatness that which he loved.” On the words of Allah “ No mortal eyes can see Him, but He can see all eyes. He is All-kind and All-aware. [6:103]
